tier_justification: Standard result of the lattice theory of up-to techniques (Pous 2007, 2016), restated for Prop-valued relations with gfp defined as the union of post-fixpoints.
plain_claim: For a monotone functional b on relations, an up-to function f that is monotone and satisfies f (b R) ⊑ b (f R) for every R is sound: every R with R ⊑ b (f R) is contained in gfp b.

hypotheses.name: hb : MonoRel b
hypotheses.purpose: Used to push each iterate fⁿ R under b, so that the union of the iterates is a post-fixpoint of b. Tight: the counterexample has a monotone f commuting with b, and f is not sound.
hypotheses.witness_class: a synthetic antitone functional (negB) on relations over the 1-element state type Unit, with f = the constant-empty function

hypotheses.name: hf : MonoRel f
hypotheses.purpose: Used to iterate the commutation (fⁿ (b R) ⊑ b (fⁿ R)); part of Pous's definition of compatibility. Tight: the counterexample has a monotone b and an f commuting with it, and f is not sound.
hypotheses.witness_class: a synthetic monotone functional (shiftB) with a non-monotone up-to function (pickF), on relations over the 2-element state type Bool

hypotheses.name: hc : Commutes b f
hypotheses.purpose: The semi-commutation f ∘ b ⊑ b ∘ f. Tight: with b monotone and f monotone, up to the total relation is not sound for strong bisimulation.
hypotheses.witness_class: the strong functional sb of the finite process LTS over two labels, with f = the constant-total function (the proof uses R = {(a.0, a.a.0)})

nonvacuity_witness: b = strong bisimulation functional of the toy process language, f = the constant function returning strong bisimilarity; the relation {(a.(0+0), a.0)} is not a strong bisimulation but progresses to f of itself.
non_claims: Compatibility is sufficient, not necessary, for soundness: weak bisimulation up to expansion is sound for wb on every transition system (weak_upto_expansion_sound) but not compatible with wb on the process LTS over any label type (weak_upto_expansion_not_compatible; card weak-upto-expansion-not-compatible).

Sound up-to functions are not closed under composition in general, even for monotone and extensive functions (not proved here; known from the Agda development nad/up-to, ¬-∘-closure, and Pous and Sangiorgi (2011, Section 6.5.4) discuss an instance). This package proves closure only for compatible functions (cards compatible-closed-under-composition, -union, -iteration) and mechanizes no counterexample for sound ones.
Does not cover functionals on lattices other than Prop-valued binary relations on one state type, nor non-monotone b.

Compatibility here is Pous's first-order notion. Respectful functions (Sangiorgi 1998) and functions below the companion (second-order) are larger classes of sound functions; they are not formalized here.

Homogeneous relations only: Rel S relates states of a single type S. Simulations between different source and target systems (S₁ → S₂ → Prop) are not modelled; closures such as the equivalence or symmetric closure, which relate states of one type, have no direct analogue there (not examined here).

Toy model only: Prop-valued binary relations on an arbitrary state type, an arbitrary labelled transition system with labels Option L (none = silent step), and, for concrete examples, a finite process syntax with only inaction, prefix and binary choice (no recursion, parallel composition, restriction or name passing).
Any application to a real proof (for example a forward or backward simulation in a compiler-correctness development) is a separate modeling-bridge argument, not established by this theorem.

hypotheses.witness_class: relations over the 1-element state type Unit (b = const ∅, f = const ⊤, g = id)

hypotheses.witness_class: relations over the 1-element state type Unit (b = const ∅, f = id, g = const ⊤)

tier_justification: The Sangiorgi-Milner pitfall, with the standard one-pair counterexample, restated and kernel-checked.
plain_claim: Over the finite process LTS with two visible labels (PStep on Proc Lbl), weak bisimulation up to weak bisimilarity (R ↦ ≈R≈) is not sound for the strong-challenge/weak-response functional wb: the one-pair relation R = {(τ.a.0, 0)} satisfies R ⊑ wb (≈R≈) (the τ-move of τ.a.0 is answered by 0 standing still, and a.0 ≈ τ.a.0 R 0 ≈ 0), yet τ.a.0 ≉ 0. Consequently ≈R≈ is not a sound technique for wb over labelled transition systems in general. The sound variants proved in this package, each with its exact hypotheses, are listed under positive_control.
nonvacuity_witness: Not applicable (counterexample); the witness relation pitfallRel is exposed in the statement.
positive_control: Witness-level controls: the same relation progresses neither to ~R~ nor to ≳R≲ under wb (pitfall_control_strong, pitfall_control_expansion). General controls (sound variants, with exact hypotheses): (1) for every LTS T, ≈R≈ is compatible with and sound for the weak-challenge functional wbWeak T (weak_challenge_upto_weak_bisim_compatible, weak_challenge_upto_weak_bisim_sound; non-vacuity weak_challenge_upto_weak_bisim_useful); (2) for every LTS T with no silent transitions (NoTau T), ≈R≈ is sound for wb T (weak_upto_weak_bisim_sound_of_noTau; non-vacuity noTau_nonvacuity); (3) for every LTS whose visible-label type is empty, every up-to function is sound for wb (sound_wb_of_no_visible; non-vacuity no_visible_nonvacuity); (4) for every LTS T, ~R~ is compatible with and sound for wb T (card weak-upto-strong-bisimilarity); (5) for every LTS T, ≳R≲ is sound for wb T (card weak-upto-expansion), and the asymmetric form (≳R≈ for left moves, ≈R≲ for right moves) is sound (card weak-upto-expansion-asymmetric); (6) for every LTS T, R ∪ ≈ is compatible with and sound for wb T (card strong-upto-union-with-bisimilarity).
non_claims: Concerns wb with strong (single-step) challenges. With weak challenges (wbWeak: p =l̂⇒ p' answered by q =l̂⇒ q'), ≈R≈ is compatible and sound, and gfp (wbWeak T) = ≈ (weak_challenge_upto_weak_bisim_compatible, weak_challenge_upto_weak_bisim_sound, gfp_wbWeak_eq_wbisim); the pitfall relation does not progress there (pitfall_not_progress_wbWeak). Of the two weak functionals defined here, the failure occurs for wb (single-step challenges) and not for wbWeak.

Does not say that every use of ≈ inside an up-to function is unsound: ~R~ and ≳R≲ are sound for wb on every transition system (weak_upto_strong_bisim_sound, weak_upto_expansion_sound), and so is the asymmetric ≳R≈ / ≈R≲ form (weak_upto_expansion_asymmetric_sound).
Does not say ≈ is not transitive or not an equivalence (≈ is symmetric and transitive here: wbisim_symm, wbisim_trans); it is only the proof technique ≈R≈ for wb that fails.

tier_justification: Pous 2016's companion, restated (union of all compatible functions).
plain_claim: For a monotone functional b, the companion of b (pointwise union of all monotone functions commuting with b) is itself compatible with b and sound for b. For every b, monotone or not, every monotone function commuting with b is below the companion (companion_greatest), and companion b ∅ = gfp b (both inclusions).

Whether up to expansion (not compatible with wb) lies below the companion of wb is not established here. The Agda development nad/up-to proves that up to expansion is size-preserving and that size-preserving functions are exactly those below the companion, which gives it there; this is not formalized here.

The companion is not monotone in the functional: although sb PStep R ⊑ wb PStep R for every R, the companion of sb is not below the companion of wb on the process LTS over two labels, since SumClo lies below the former but is not sound for wb there (companion_not_monotone_in_functional). Membership below the companion of sb says nothing about the weak case.
